To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cognitive processes involved with online document-based information search are (a) the use of a hierarchical search strategy; (b) the use of the document title to identify relevant documents and to select the most appropriate document to view; and (c) the use of an “integrated” strategy for document viewing.
the cognitive process of document retrieval involves the use of multiple cognitive processes that can be modeled as a series of stages.

the cognitive processes underlying document-based online retrieval are (1) the construction of a representation of the document and (2) a search for a representation of the query in the document representation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing computational models of the cognitive processes that are used by people in the process of online document-based information seeking, and with incorporating these models into the design of intelligent document-based retrieval systems.
the design of intelligent retrieval systems that can support users in their information-seeking activities.

developing an understanding of the cognitive processes involved during online document-based information seeking, and using this knowledge to develop an “intelligent”, document-based retrieval system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cognitive processes involved are complex and that the retrieval process is a function of the user’s goals.
our work has shown that the design of intelligent information retrieval systems must take into account the cognitive processes of the user.
cognitive process as a basis of intelligent retrieval systems design has been a successful endeavor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cognitive process of online document-based information search and retrieval can be modeled and that these models can be used to design intelligent retrieval systems.

we have developed a theoretical framework for understanding the cognitive processes involved during document-based information retrieval and that this framework has led to the development, implementation, and evaluation of an “integrated” document-based retrieval model.
the design of intelligent retrieval systems requires an understanding of the cognitive processes underlying information retrieval and the development of computational models of these processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cognitive processes that underpin online document retrieval are highly complex, but that these processes can be modeled and simulated.

the design of intelligent information retrieval systems should not be based on the assumption that users will always be able to express their information needs using the same vocabulary as that of the documents in the database.
cognitive processes should be used as a basis for the design of intelligent information retrieval systems.
